currentUse: Vacant lot with adjoining former rectory, listed for sale by the Diocese of Allentown in June 2024; a Gold Star Highway billboard memorializes the church

historicalNarrative.text: St. George parish emerged from Shenandoah's Lithuanian community after eighteen organizers met on February 12, 1891 and resolved to form a separate Lithuanian parish. At a public meeting on March 31, Father Petras Abromaitis announced that permission had been obtained; by April 7 the organizers had collected more than $4,000 for the new parish, which took the name St. George.

The parish church was dedicated on May 12, 1894. It became one of the central institutions of Lithuanian life in Pennsylvania's coal region and remained the community's spiritual landmark until the Diocese of Allentown closed the parish in 2006.

Approaching the church's centennial, the parish undertook a restoration that lasted more than three years and involved more than fifteen contractors. The work renewed the stained glass, Stations of the Cross, statues, altars, organ, exterior steps, lighting, and church hall. Weekly St. George Bingo and other parish events helped raise money for the renovation; in 1992 a new steel roof, copper steeples, and crosses completed another major phase of the work.

historicalNarrative.text: In 2003 and 2004, structural engineers recommended resetting stone on the towers and facade. After pieces of the facade fell in 2006, the Diocese of Allentown closed the church on May 14. The Friends of St. George publicly argued that the parish could finance necessary work and that parish funds should have been directed to repairs; diocesan estimates later placed the work in the millions. These were disputed assessments, not a case of a community simply walking away from its church.

historicalNarrative.text: The campaign continued after the doors were locked. Supporters gathered every Wednesday to pray, sought historic protection for the building, and pressed the case through Lithuanian-American organizations. In February 2007, representatives meeting in Chicago adopted resolutions concerning Shenandoah, Niagara Falls, and Manhattan and sent them to church and civic leaders in the United States and Lithuania, asking for help preserving the parishes.

historicalNarrative.text: Parishioners went to civil court in September 2009 to challenge the Diocese's plan to demolish the church and its assertion that repair costs made preservation impossible. On December 1, the court held that the plaintiffs had no property right allowing them to block the Diocese. Demolition began that month. The loss therefore followed years of repair work, fundraising, organizing, public appeals, and litigation—not abandonment by the people who had maintained St. George.

summary: The church was razed in 2009 and its site on South Jardin Street remains a vacant lot. In June 2024 the Diocese of Allentown, through Divine Mercy Parish, listed the lot bundled with the former rectory for $139,900, with proceeds to the parish. A billboard along the Gold Star Highway reminds motorists of the lost landmark, and heritage advocates funded a commemorative plaque for Shenandoah's 'Little Lithuania' after the diocese reneged on a promised symbolic belfry. Salvaged stained glass from St. George's is now displayed at the Lithuanian Heritage Museum, which opened September 7, 2025 at 318 East Centre Street in a former family funeral home, open by appointment. The Lithuanian Days festival, America's oldest continuous ethnic festival, continues at Lakewood Park in Barnesville, with the 2026 edition set for August 15-16 and proceeds benefiting the museum.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: LRT states the church was 'closed by the local diocese in 2010,' conflating closure (2006) with demolition (2009). Global True Lithuania corroborates the reneged belfry promise (stones stored at Our Lady of Calvary Cemetery) and notes heritage-listing funds went instead to a commemorative plaque — a memorial element not in the archive record.

No recent open-web coverage found on the current condition or maintenance of the St. George/oldest Lithuanian cemetery. The ~$1M savings transfer and the Dec 2016 bells-to-Houston transfer were not independently verified in non-Draugas sources opened for this search.
